data.name: Cirrhosis Patient Survival Prediction
data.abstract: Utilize 17 clinical features for predicting survival state of patients with liver cirrhosis. The survival states include 0 = D (death), 1 = C (censored), 2 = CL (censored due to liver transplantation).

intro_paper.title: Prognosis in primary biliary cirrhosis: Model for decision making
intro_paper.authors: E. Dickson, P. Grambsch, T. Fleming, L. Fisher, A. Langworthy

variables.name: N_Days
variables.description: number of days between registration and the earlier of death, transplantation, or study analysis time in July 1986

variables.name: Status
variables.description: status of the patient C (censored), CL (censored due to liver tx), or D (death)

variables.name: Drug
variables.description: type of drug D-penicillamine or placebo

variables.name: Ascites
variables.description: presence of ascites N (No) or Y (Yes)

variables.name: Hepatomegaly
variables.description: presence of hepatomegaly N (No) or Y (Yes)

variables.name: Spiders
variables.description: presence of spiders N (No) or Y (Yes)

variables.name: Edema
variables.description: presence of edema N (no edema and no diuretic therapy for edema), S (edema present without diuretics, or edema resolved by diuretics), or Y (edema despite diuretic therapy)

additional_info.summary: During 1974 to 1984, 424 PBC patients referred to the Mayo Clinic qualified for the randomized placebo-controlled trial testing the drug D-penicillamine. Of these, the initial 312 patients took part in the trial and have mostly comprehensive data. The remaining 112 patients didn't join the clinical trial but agreed to record basic metrics and undergo survival tracking. Six of these patients were soon untraceable after their diagnosis, leaving data for 106 of these individuals in addition to the 312 who were part of the randomized trial.
additional_info.purpose: Cirrhosis results from prolonged liver damage, leading to extensive scarring, often due to conditions like hepatitis or chronic alcohol consumption. The data provided is sourced from a Mayo Clinic study on primary biliary cirrhosis (PBC) of the liver carried out from 1974 to 1984.
additional_info.preprocessing_description:
1. Drop all the rows where miss value (NA) were present in the Drug column
2. Impute missing values with mean results
3. One-hot encoding for all category attributes
additional_info.variable_info:
1. ID: unique identifier
2. N_Days: number of days between registration and the earlier of death, transplantation, or study analysis time in July 1986
3. Status: status of the patient C (censored), CL (censored due to liver tx), or D (death)
4. Drug: type of drug D-penicillamine or placebo
5. Age: age in [days]
6. Sex: M (male) or F (female)
7. Ascites: presence of ascites N (No) or Y (Yes)
8. Hepatomegaly: presence of hepatomegaly N (No) or Y (Yes)
9. Spiders: presence of spiders N (No) or Y (Yes)
10. Edema: presence of edema N (no edema and no diuretic therapy for edema), S (edema present without diuretics, or edema resolved by diuretics), or Y (edema despite diuretic therapy)
11. Bilirubin: serum bilirubin in [mg/dl]
12. Cholesterol: serum cholesterol in [mg/dl]
13. Albumin: albumin in [gm/dl]
14. Copper: urine copper in [ug/day]
15. Alk_Phos: alkaline phosphatase in [U/liter]
16. SGOT: SGOT in [U/ml]
17. Triglycerides: triglicerides in [mg/dl]
18. Platelets: platelets per cubic [ml/1000]
19. Prothrombin: prothrombin time in seconds [s]
20. Stage: histologic stage of disease (1, 2, 3, or 4)
additional_info.citation: Fleming, Thomas R., and David P. Harrington. Counting processes and survival analysis. Vol. 625. John Wiley & Sons, 2013.
